blocks.heading: The format
lines: 4 passages of about 400 to 600 words, 4 questions each: 16 of the 24 VARC questions.
All multiple choice: +3 right, minus 1 wrong.
Start with 3 passages at about 9 minutes each. The fourth only pays once three take under 28 minutes.

blocks.heading: 1. Pick the passage (30 seconds each)
lines: Read the first two lines and the four question stems.
Prefer a topic you can follow and questions that point to the text ("according to the passage", a quoted phrase).
Leave for last the passage whose first lines you had to read twice.

blocks.heading: 2. Read once, for the structure (3 to 4 minutes)
lines: After each paragraph, say in five words what it does: "old view", "attacks it", "an example", "author's answer".
Mark the author's own position. Words like however, yet, surprisingly, it is doubtful show where it is.
Don't stop to learn details. A question will send you back to them.

blocks.heading: 3. Answer each question (about 1 minute)
lines: Name the type: detail, inference, main idea or purpose, the author's view or tone, EXCEPT, or apply to a new case.
For main idea and tone, say your answer in your own words before you read the options.
For detail and inference, go back to the lines it refers to and read the sentence before and after.
Cut options, don't hunt for the right one. Down to two, find the one word in each that the passage doesn't support.

blocks.heading: Options that are usually wrong
lines: True in the real world, but not said in the passage.
Half right: the first part matches, the second part adds or reverses something.
Too strong: always, only, never, entirely, when the passage hedges.
Too narrow: one paragraph's point offered as the main idea. Or too broad: a whole field when the passage covers one case.
A view the author reports from others, offered as the author's own.
Two parts of the passage joined into a claim it never makes, such as a cause it doesn't state.

blocks.heading: When to answer and when to leave it
lines: Answer when you're down to two options: on average that gains marks.
Leave it blank when three or four still look possible after a minute.
If a passage's first two questions both stall you, leave it and use the time on the next passage.

blocks.heading: After each practice passage
lines: For every miss, write which wrong-option type caught you.
For every right answer, say which line proves it. A lucky guess counts as a miss.
Two weeks of this does more than reading extra passages without review.
